source_text:
Καὶ παρεγένοντο οἱ ἄνδρες οἳ ἦσαν ἀκάθαρτοι ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο ποιῆσαι τὸ Πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. Καὶ προσῆλθον ἐναντίον Μωσῆ καὶ Ἀαρὼν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἄνδρες ἐκεῖνοι πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἡμεῖς ἀκάθαρτοι ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, μὴ οὖν ὑστερήσωμεν προσενέγκαι τὸ δῶρον Κυρίῳ κατὰ καιρὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν μέσῳ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ. Καὶ εἶπε πρὸς αὐτοὺς Μωσῆς· Στῆτε αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκούσομαι τί ἐντελεῖται Κύριος περὶ ὑμῶν. Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, λέγων· Ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἐὰν γένηται ἀκάθαρτος ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, ἢ ἐν ὁδῷ μακρὰν ὑμῖν, ἢ ἐν ταῖς γενεαῖς ὑμῶν, καὶ ποιήσει τὸ Πάσχα Κυρίῳ· ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ δευτέρῳ ἐν τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ, τὸ πρὸς ἑσπέραν ποιήσουσιν αὐτὸ, ἐπ' ἀζύμων καὶ πικρίδων τῇ νυκτὶ φάγονται αὐτὸ, οὐ καταλείψουσιν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πρωῒ, καὶ ὀστοῦν οὐ συντρίψουσιν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ. Κατὰ τὸν νόμον τοῦ Πάσχα ποιήσουσιν αὐτό. Καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἐὰν καθαρὸς ᾖ, καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ μακρὰν οὐκ ἔστι, καὶ ὑστερήσῃ ποιῆσαι τὸ Πάσχα, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτῆς, ὅτι τὸ δῶρον Κυρίῳ οὐ προσήνεγκε κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν αὐτοῦ, ἁμαρτίαν αὐτοῦ λήψεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος. Ἐὰν δὲ προσέλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς προσήλυτος ἐν τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν, καὶ ποιήσῃ τὸ Πάσχα Κυρίῳ κατὰ τὸν νόμον τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ κατὰ τὴν σύνταξιν αὐτοῦ, οὕτω ποιήσει αὐτὸ, νόμος εἷς ἔσται ὑμῖν, καὶ τῷ προσηλύτῳ, καὶ τῷ αὐτόχθονι τῆς γῆς.»
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τίνες ἂν εἶεν οἱ ἀκάθαρτοι μὲν ὡς ἐπ' ἀνθρώπου ψυχῇ, πρόφασιν δὲ τοῦ μὴ δύνασθαι τὸ Πάσχα πληροῦν τὸ χρῆμα ποιούμενοι, βουλοίμην ἂν εἰδέναι σαφῶς, ὡς εὖ ἴσθι τοι.
{ΚΥΡ.} Πολὺς μὲν δὴ λίαν τῆς ἱστορίας ὁ λόγος. Μεμνήσομαι γὰρ διακεκραγότος Θεοῦ πρὸς τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωσέα· «Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐξαποστειλάτωσαν ἐκ τῆς παρεμβολῆς πάντα λεπρὸν καὶ πάντα γονοῤῥυῆ, καὶ πάντα ἀκάθαρτον ἐπὶ ψυχῇ.» Καὶ ἅλις μὲν ἡμῖν ὁ περὶ τουτωνὶ πεπόνηται λόγος. Πλὴν ἐκεῖνό φημι χρησίμως εἰς τὸ παρόν. Ἀκάθαρτον μὲν γὰρ ἐπ' ἀνθρώπου ψυχῇ τὸ Γράμμα λέγει τὸ ἱερὸν, τὸν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ μεμολυσμένον· ἀπείρηται γὰρ καὶ ἀψύχου σώματος ἀποθίγειν, καὶ τοῖς πενθοῦσί τινα τῶν ἀγχοῦ καὶ ἐξ αἵματος τῆς ἀκαθαρσίας τὴν γραφὴν τὸ ἀρχαῖον ἐπετίθει θέσπισμα. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἐξεπέμποντο τῆς παρεμβολῆς. Ὑπετύπου δὲ αὖ διὰ τούτων ὁ νόμος, ὡς ἀνίερος ἔσται τις καὶ νοητῆς ἀκαθαρσίας ἔμπλεως, τῆς ἑτέρου νεκρότητος μετεσχηκὼς, ὡς ἐν ἤθει τε καὶ τρόποις· νεκροὶ γὰρ τοὺς τρόπους οἱ περὶ ὧν ἂν λέγοιτο παρὰ Χριστοῦ «Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάπτειν τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς.» Ἔξω δὴ οὖν τῆς θείας αὐλῆς, καὶ τῆς τῶν πρωτοτόκων Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγέλης ἀπόπεμπτος, ὁ τοῖς τὰ νεκρὰ φρονεῖν τε καὶ δρᾷν εἰωθόσι κεκοινωνηκὼς, ἢ καὶ ἀγχοῦ γεγονὼς, κατά γε τὸ ἑλέσθαι φημὶ τὰ ἴσα φρονεῖν τε καὶ δρᾷν. Ἀλλ' ὧδε μὲν ἔχει τοῦ νόμου τὸ αἴνιγμα. Πρὸς διάνοιαν δὲ τὴν ἀληθῆ, καὶ ὅτι μάλιστα τὴν πρεπωδεστάτην ἡμῖν τοῖς πνευματικοῖς, τοὺς ἀκαθάρτους ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, ταύτῃ τοι καὶ ἐν μηνὶ
pass_a_gloss: And the men came who were unclean on (account of) a soul of a man, and were not able to make the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron on that day, and those men said to him: We are unclean on a soul of a man; let us not then fall behind in offering the gift to the Lord according to its season in the midst of the sons of Israel. And Moses said to them: Stand there and I will hear what the Lord will command about you. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the sons of Israel saying: A man, whoever becomes unclean on a soul of a man, or in a road far for you, or in your generations, and will make the Passover to the Lord: in the second month on the fourteenth day, the toward-evening they will make it, on unleavened (breads) and bitter herbs in the night they will eat it, they will not leave from it to the morning, and a bone they will not break from it. According to the law of the Passover they will make it. And a man, whoever is clean and is not in a road far, and falls behind to make the Passover, that soul will be destroyed out of its people, because he did not bring the gift to the Lord according to its season, that man will take his sin. And if a proselyte comes to you in your land and makes the Passover to the Lord according to the law of the Passover and according to its arrangement, thus he will make it; one law will be for you, both for the proselyte and for the native of the land. PALLADIUS: And who would be those unclean as on a man's soul, and making the matter a pretext for not being able to fulfill the Passover, I would wish to know clearly, know it well. CYRIL: Very much indeed is the account of the history. For I will remember God having cried out to the hierophant Moses: Speak to the sons of Israel and let them send out of the camp every leper and every one flowing with seed, and every one unclean on a soul. And enough has been labored by us about these. Except that I say this usefully for the present: for the sacred Letter calls unclean on a man's soul the one defiled on a dead body; for it has been forbidden even to touch a soulless body, and the ancient decree laid the charge of uncleanness on those mourning some one of those near and of blood. Therefore also they were sent out of the camp. And through these the law sketched beforehand that someone will be unholy and full of intelligible (spiritual) uncleanness, having shared in another's deadness, as in character and ways; for dead in ways are those about whom it would be said by Christ: Let the dead bury their own dead. So outside the divine court and of the Church of the firstborn and of the herd of the saints (is) to-be-sent-away the one who has shared with those used to thinking and doing the dead things, or has even come near, I mean in choosing to think and do equal things. But thus holds the riddle of the law. And toward the true understanding and the one most fitting for us the spiritual ones, those unclean on a soul of a man, therefore also in the month (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … ‘And there came the men who were unclean through a human soul, and they could not keep the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron on that day, and those men said to him: We are unclean through a human soul; must we then be kept back from offering the gift to the Lord at its season among the sons of Israel? And Moses said to them: Stand here, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: Any man who becomes unclean through a human soul, or is on a journey far from you, or among your generations, and would keep the Passover to the Lord: in the second month, on the fourteenth day, toward evening, they shall keep it; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it by night; they shall leave none of it until morning, and they shall not break a bone of it. According to the law of the Passover they shall keep it. And the man who is clean and is not on a journey far away, and fails to keep the Passover, that soul shall be destroyed from its people, because he did not offer the gift to the Lord at its season; that man shall bear his sin. And if a proselyte comes to you in your land and keeps the Passover to the Lord according to the law of the Passover and according to its ordinance, so shall he keep it. There shall be one law for you, both for the proselyte and for the native of the land’ (Numbers 9:6–14).
Palladius: And who might they be, who are unclean as through a human soul and make this a pretext for not being able to keep the Passover? I should like to know clearly, you may be sure.

Cyril: The account of the history is a very long one. I will recall God crying out to Moses, the revealer of sacred things: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them send out of the camp every leper and everyone who has a discharge, and everyone unclean through a soul’ (Numbers 5:2). We have already labored over the account of these things enough. But I will say this, as useful for the present. By ‘unclean through a human soul’ the sacred letter means the one defiled by a corpse. For it was forbidden even to touch a lifeless body, and the ancient decree laid the charge of uncleanness on those mourning one of their near kin and blood. That is why they were sent out of the camp. And by these things the law foreshadowed that whoever has shared in another’s deadness, in character and ways, will be unholy and full of spiritual uncleanness. For those are dead in their ways of whom Christ would say, ‘Let the dead bury their own dead’ (Matthew 8:22). So the one who has shared with those used to thinking and doing dead things, or has even come near them (I mean by choosing to think and do the same), is to be sent outside the divine court, and the Church of the firstborn (Hebrews 12:23), and the flock of the saints. Such, then, is the riddle of the law. But by the true sense, and the one most fitting for us who are spiritual, those unclean through a human soul, who for this reason keep the feast in the …

lemmas.gloss: unclean through a human soul (by a corpse)

choices.why: The Septuagint idiom is kept close, because Cyril goes on to explain it (‘the one defiled by a corpse’); a smooth rendering would make his explanation pointless.

choices.english: Moses, the revealer of sacred things
choices.why: ἱεροφάντης, one who shows sacred things; not ‘high priest’.
The phrase is split at the column break; ‘second month’ is rendered once, at the start of §12.
